stem: The IP camera cam-01 has a web page. Which web server software does its Server header name?
explain: curl -I http://cam-01 shows Server: Boa/0.94.14rc21. Boa is an embedded web server that has not been maintained since 2005 and has known vulnerabilities, a typical weakness of cheap cameras and other IoT devices. Banner reading is the first step of identifying what is exposed; the finding is to isolate or replace the device. (cam-01 also has telnet open.)

stem: Which line names the web server software on the camera?

options.why: That is the type of the page.
That is the size of the body.

explain: The Server header announces the software and version. Boa is a small server found in embedded devices.

stem: What should an assessor note about 'Boa/0.94.14rc21' on an IP camera?

options.text: Old embedded web software is exposed and may have known vulnerabilities
Nothing, because cameras never run web servers of their own, only firmware
options.why: This one does, and the header proves it.

options.text: The camera's traffic is encrypted end to end by default
options.why: A plain http response shows no encryption.

options.text: The camera is also acting as the domain controller for the site
options.why: The header says nothing about that.

explain: Embedded devices often run outdated software that is rarely patched. Find the version, then check the vendor for fixes or isolate the device.

stem: What does 'Failed to connect to 192.168.10.1:80' tell you?

options.text: The gateway is certainly powered off, because its web server refused us
options.why: A failed connection on one port does not show that.

options.text: Port 80 refused or did not answer; that alone does not prove the host is down
The web server answered, but with a 404 error for the page that was requested
options.why: A 404 would mean a server answered.

options.text: The DNS lookup failed because the name could not be resolved
options.why: The address was given as numbers, so no lookup was needed.

explain: curl error 7 means the TCP connection could not be made: the port is closed or filtered. Another port, such as 443, may well be open.

stem: According to the file, where does this PC get its gateway and DNS settings?

options.text: They are typed in by hand on each PC
options.why: The readme says they come from DHCP.
The file does not mention it.
The file does not mention it.

explain: type prints a text file. Reading local notes is often the quickest way to learn how a machine is set up.

stem: Which Windows command prints the contents of a text file, like cat on Linux?
explain: type readme.txt prints the file. The Linux counterpart is cat.

stem: Which Windows command searches text for a string, like grep on Linux?
explain: findstr prints the lines that contain a string, for example: findstr DHCP readme.txt.
